facts.text: Pedagogy is the theory and practice of teaching. It encompasses the strategies, methods, and approaches educators use to facilitate learning. Key theorists: Comenius, Pestalozzi, Froebel, Dewey, Piaget, Vygotsky.
Bloom's Taxonomy (Benjamin Bloom, 1956, revised by Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001) classifies educational learning objectives into 6 levels: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create.

Constructivism is a learning theory (Piaget, Vygotsky) arguing that learners actively construct knowledge through experiences and reflection, rather than passively receiving information. Key concepts: scaffolding, zone of proximal development (ZPD).
Montessori education (Maria Montessori, early 1900s) emphasizes self-directed activity, hands-on learning, and collaborative play. Mixed-age classrooms, specially designed materials.

Differentiated instruction (Carol Ann Tomlinson) tailors teaching to individual student needs — content, process, product, or learning environment adjusted based on student readiness, interest, or learning profile.
Formative assessment is ongoing assessment used to monitor student learning and provide feedback during instruction. Contrast with summative assessment (end-of-term, evaluative).

facts.text: Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD, Vygotsky) is the gap between what a learner can do independently and what they can do with guidance. Scaffolding bridges this gap.
Giáo dục là quá trình đào tạo con người thông qua việc truyền thụ kiến thức, kỹ năng, và giá trị. Ba loại hình: giáo dục chính quy, thường xuyên, tự học.
Flipped Classroom inverts traditional teaching: students learn content at home (videos, readings), and class time is used for active learning, discussion, problem-solving.
STEM education integrates Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics. Extended as STEAM (adds Arts). Emphasizes interdisciplinary, applied approach.
